Subject: Proposed MSA amendments re: title of output and training prohibition

Laura —

Thanks for the demo and the follow-up. Attached is a redline of your standard MSA (NovaCorp_Redline_v1.docx) with a couple of asks we need to close for procurement and legal sign-off:

1) Title to Output: NovaCorp requests explicit assignment of title for Customer Outputs (defined as productized text/images produced from NovaCorp input and prompts) so we can commercially exploit outputs without downstream license risk.
2) Training/Model Use: NovaCorp requires a prohibition on using Customer Content (including outputs) to train or fine-tune Redwood models or derivative products; telemetry/metrics for diagnostics may be permitted but only in anonymized, aggregated form and subject to opt-out.
3) Feedback License: Any feedback we provide during the engagement must be limited and non-exclusive, and cannot be used to create a model that is transferred or commercialized with NovaCorp-derived behavior.
4) Evidence & Auditability: Procurement asks for clear operational controls + a process for evidence (logs/telemetry) proving Customer Content is not used for training.

We appreciate that some of these asks may be outside your standard position. Please let us know Redwood's counterproposal so the teams can decide whether to proceed to signature or request a PO hold.

Laura / Marissa —

High-level legal position and recommended compromise:

1) Definitions & Narrow Assignment: We can accept assignment of title if we narrowly define "Customer Outputs" (e.g., "Outputs that are direct verbatim expressions of Customer Content or otherwise uniquely attributable to Customer prompts and not to pre-existing model behavior"). This protects Redwood from inadvertent over-assigning title for generic model generations.

2) Training / Model Use: We must retain the right to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry to operate and improve the service. However, we can agree not to use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or fine-tune models that would be applied back to NovaCorp or other customers in a manner that would reproduce proprietary NovaCorp content. Proposed contract language: prohibit training on Customer Content and Customer Outputs, but allow a separate limited "Operational Telemetry" carve-in for monitoring/bug fixes. Also include an option box in the Order Form Annex where NovaCorp can opt-in to a paid "Model Improvements" license if they want Redwood to use anonymized contributions to improve the general model.

3) Feedback License: Make it explicit that feedback is non-exclusive and non-proprietary in a narrow way (allowing aggregation into general improvements but not attributable to NovaCorp). We'll add a clause prohibiting creation of models that replicate NovaCorp-specific behavior if feedback is derived from Customer Content.

4) Auditability & Evidence: We can offer an operational compliance bundle: (a) attestation annually, (b) sampled telemetry export for customer review under NDA, (c) retention policy and data deletion timeline. Full forensic audit would be scoped as a paid professional services engagement.

I'll prepare a counter-redline (Redwood_Counterproposal_v1.docx) that: (i) adds a narrowly scoped definition of Customer Outputs, (ii) adds the training prohibition but preserves operational telemetry, (iii) creates an Order Form Annex template that documents opt-out/opt-in for model improvements and pricing.

Next steps: I'll circulate the redline this afternoon. If NovaCorp insists on full assignment without narrow definition, we should escalate to execs — that's a product/legal tradeoff with long-term implications.

-Karthik

Amelia / David —

Thanks for the redline and for outlining NovaCorp's priorities. We've reviewed internally and want to propose a pragmatic path forward to keep the procurement timeline on track. Summary of Redwood's counterproposal below; I attached a clean Order Form Annex so your team can see the mechanics.

Proposal (short):
- Title to "Customer Outputs": Redwood will grant NovaCorp exclusive title to Customer Outputs produced solely from NovaCorp inputs under the Order Form, subject to a narrowly worded definition (see attached Annex). This is intended to allow NovaCorp to productize outputs without broad assignment of model IP.
- Training / Model Use: Redwood agrees not to use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or fine-tune models used in service to NovaCorp or shared customers, except where NovaCorp explicitly opts into a paid "Model Improvements" license in the Annex. Redwood retains the right to use aggregated and de-identified telemetry for diagnostic and operational improvements.
- Feedback License: Any feedback provided will be non-exclusive and limited; Redwood will not create or distribute a model that reproduces NovaCorp-specific outputs.
- Evidence & Audit: We will provide an annual attestation and offer a scoped telemetry sample under NDA; full forensic audits can be procured as a billable service.

If that direction is acceptable, our legal team (Karthik) will send the formal counter-redline (Redwood_Counterproposal_v1.docx) and the Annex (OrderForm_Annex_Draft.pdf) via DocuSign for acceptance. Commercially, Marissa has proposed a modest uplift (15–25%) tied to opting out of model improvements; we can incorporate pricing into the Annex.

Would NovaCorp be ok with a short call tomorrow to walk the Annex and pricing? If you want to proceed straight to doc exchange, Karthik will circulate the counterproposal this afternoon.
